pricingNotice: Pricing, availability, and model behavior change frequently. Confirm current details in official vendor documentation before choosing a model or making a purchase decision.

openai.name: OpenAI
openai.blurb: Flexible reasoning controls for fast, everyday, and quality first work.

anthropic.name: Anthropic
anthropic.blurb: Strong agents and sustained reasoning for demanding work.

xai.name: xAI
xai.blurb: A capable general option with large context choices.

google.name: Google
google.blurb: Fast multimodal work, agent support, and on device options.

astra.name: GPT-6 Astra
astra.text: The OpenAI ceiling for hardest end-to-end work, especially computer use, browsing, and production-critical delivery. Not an effort tick on Sol. Stay on Sol unless Extra High or Pro already failed a representative eval.
uses: Operating desktop or web apps without an API
Final production or client reviews where Sol Pro is not enough
astra.moveUp: There is no higher OpenAI rung in this desk. If Astra is the wrong shape, change labs rather than adding effort.

sol.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
sol.text: The starting point for normal professional work on OpenAI. Raise effort before you change model. Instant for short polish, High when several sources appear, Extra High or Pro when failure is costly, then Astra.
uses: Writing, planning, reports, and everyday coding
Research with several sources at High
Quality-first 5.6 delivery at Extra High or Pro
sol.moveUp: Move to Astra when Sol Extra High or Sol Pro is visibly falling short, or the job is computer use.

terra.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
terra.text: The cost-conscious production successor to GPT-5.5. Use for repeated professional workflows, spreadsheet analysis, and routine coding. Compare against Sol before you standardise Extra High here.
uses: Document processing at volume with some judgment
terra.moveUp: Move to Sol High when the work needs architecture, causal reasoning, or unfamiliar tradeoffs.

luna.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
luna.text: The cheap 5.6 tier for clean, well-defined extraction, classification, and batch transforms. List pricing now sits in the high-volume band. Do not push Luna to Extra High across a whole batch.
luna.moveUp: Move to Terra when exceptions, formulas, or business rules appear. Skip Luna Extra High.

gpt55.name: GPT-5.5
gpt55.text: Keep only for prompts already validated on 5.5. New work should start on Terra or Sol after an A/B on accuracy, latency, and cost.
gpt55.moveUp: Migrate to Terra or Sol only after a side-by-side eval. Quality-first new work belongs on Sol Pro or Astra.

fable51.name: Claude Fable 5.1
fable51.text: Successor to Fable 5 for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agents. Anthropic still says start on Opus 5. Use Fable 5.1 when Opus at higher effort falls short. Default effort is high. Thinking is adaptive and always on.
uses: Hardest document, spreadsheet, and slide work
Cases where Opus 5 already failed evals
fable51.moveUp: Raise to xhigh or max only when evals show headroom. Mythos 5.1 is invitation-only.

opus5.name: Claude Opus 5
opus5.text: The quality-first Claude default for complex agentic coding and enterprise work. Start at high. Use xhigh for long coding runs. Effort is not a length control.
opus5.moveUp: Move to Fable 5.1 at high when Opus 5 is visibly falling short.

sonnet5.name: Claude Sonnet 5
sonnet5.text: The practical Claude route for production agents at volume. Start at high. Medium is a documented cost-saving step-down, close to Sonnet 4.6 at high.
uses: Production agents and coding at volume
Complex reasoning where turnaround still matters
Most Claude app and API workloads
sonnet5.moveUp: Move to Opus 5 at high when quality is the point. xhigh on Sonnet is for hard coding before you pay Opus rates.

haiku45.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
haiku45.text: Fastest Claude with near-frontier intelligence for classify, route, extract, and subagents. The effort parameter is not supported. Use budget_tokens if you need extended thinking.
haiku45.moveUp: Move to Sonnet 5 when the step needs real judgment or multi-step coding.

fable5.name: Claude Fable 5
fable5.text: Previous Fable ceiling. New work should use Fable 5.1 at high and re-sweep effort. Do not copy Fable 5 xhigh defaults onto 5.1 without evals.
fable5.moveUp: Move new work to Fable 5.1. Keep this card only for compatibility.

grok46.name: Grok 4.6
grok46.text: Official start for almost everything on xAI: chat, research, coding, and agents. 500k context. Configurable reasoning from low to xhigh. Grok 4.7 is not generally available.
uses: Grok Build CLI default since 12 Aug 2026
grok46.moveUp: Switch to 4.3 for 1M context or lower input price. Use Build 0.1 when you want a cheaper coding-only specialist.

grok43.name: Grok 4.3
grok43.text: Reach here when the job exceeds the 4.6 500k window, or when a large input is cheaper on 4.3. 1M context.
uses: PDF, sheet, and slide generation from big sources
grok43.moveUp: Stay on 4.6 for general intelligence. Use 4.20 Reasoning or Multi-Agent only for hard multi-step exploration.

grok420.name: Grok 4.20
grok420.text: Reasoning and Multi-Agent variants for hard multi-step analysis and parallel exploration. Not the everyday default.
grok420.moveUp: Prefer 4.6 Heavy first. Use 4.20 when you specifically want the reasoning or multi-agent surface.

grokbuild.name: Grok Build 0.1
grokbuild.text: Fast, cheap coding specialist with always-on reasoning and a 256k window. The Grok Build CLI default is now 4.6; keep 0.1 when you want the coding-only price envelope.
grokbuild.moveUp: Move to Grok 4.6 when the task leaves pure coding or needs the 500k window.

grokfast.name: Grok Fast
grokfast.text: High-volume Grok variants for classification, routing, bulk summaries, and lightweight agents. Context can reach 2M on some Fast ids.
grokfast.moveUp: Move to 4.6 when the task needs judgment, coding, or agent reliability.

flash38.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
flash38.text: Current Flash default for everyday coding, agents, and multimodal work. 1M input / 64k output. Thinking levels low, medium, high. Introductory price through 31 December 2026.
uses: Broad research before a deeper lab
flash38.moveUp: Turn thinking to high, or move to 3.1 Pro, only if Flash struggles with the logic. Keep 3.7 if a path is pinned.

flash37.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
flash37.text: Previous Flash workhorse from the 22 August desk. Still stable. Re-sweep evals before a silent cutover to 3.8.
flash37.moveUp: New work should start on 3.8 Flash at the same introductory price.

flashlite.name: Gemini Flash-Lite
flashlite.text: Downgrade only when the task is simple enough that a smaller model does it perfectly and you want to shave latency and cost at massive scale.
flashlite.moveUp: Move to 3.8 Flash as soon as the task needs multi-step reasoning or coding.

live38.name: Gemini 3.8 Live
live38.text: Default Live API model for low-latency voice agents. Use Live Extended Thinking when the agent must plan before it speaks.
uses: Voice interfaces that should not wait on long reasoning
live38.moveUp: Use Extended Thinking when accuracy matters more than immediate reply. Text work still belongs on 3.8 Flash.

pro31.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
pro31.text: Upgrade only if Flash struggles with expert logic, advanced coding, or synthesis across massive inputs. Still preview.
uses: Architecture and expert logic Flash missed
pro31.moveUp: If you need a generally available ceiling, change labs rather than living on a preview.

nano.name: Gemini Nano
nano.text: Use when data must not leave the device, or when you need zero-latency offline replies. Not a cloud reasoning substitute.
nano.moveUp: Move to 3.8 Flash as soon as the work can leave the device.

balanced: A quick route for polished emails, updates, and short rewrites. Step up to Sol Medium when stakeholder dynamics or sensitivity matter.
speed: Use this for repeatable short updates where speed and cost matter most.
quality: Use this when tone, persuasion, or several stakeholders deserve extra judgment.

balanced: A reliable general route for reports, planning, spreadsheets, and everyday professional judgment.
speed: A cost conscious workhorse for repeatable professional workflows.
quality: Choose this when the deliverable needs stronger synthesis and carefully checked reasoning.

balanced: Use this for several sources, constraints, calculations, or tradeoffs.
speed: A fast route for broad research and source gathering before deeper analysis.
quality: Use this for nuanced, ambiguous, or high impact research where checking work is valuable. Move to GPT-6 Astra when computer use or end-to-end professional work is the bottleneck.

balanced: A solid starting point for routine coding, debugging, and practical implementation.
speed: A focused option for interactive coding when efficiency is the primary goal. Gemini 3.8 Flash is the Google equivalent.
quality: A strong route for architecture, large refactors, and demanding tool based coding work. Fable 5.1 or GPT-6 Astra if Opus is visibly falling short.

balanced: Use this for clean extraction, classification, routing, and batch transformations. Luna list pricing is now in the cheap high-volume band.
speed: A fast option for well defined high volume classification and extraction.
quality: Use this when exceptions, business rules, and richer validation enter the workflow.

balanced: A careful starting point for expensive mistakes, difficult ambiguity, and serious technical review.
speed: Maintain a strong reasoning baseline when time is limited, then add targeted review where risk is greatest.
quality: Reserve this for final production reviews, computer-use work, and high value deliverables where Sol Pro is no longer the ceiling.
